US: Fast-battleship bombardment, minesweeping/reef work and continuing carrier suppression make the Saipan invasion unmistakable. Fast-battleship fire causes meaningful suppression but does not systematically destroy concealed Japanese defenses. FORAGER remains on schedule.
Japan_land_air: Marianas air power conducts one bounded attack on the fixed bombardment geometry while continuing cadre preservation. End-day onsite ready 103-137, fighters 52-72, attack/recon 29-42. Local air superiority is lost, but reconnaissance and local strike capability remain.
Japan_fleet: Yamamoto closes the final A-GO gate and releases the battle force. Five-carrier core and secondary carrier group finish Guimaras concentration/refuel; eastward sortie is centered on 14 Jun. Yamato/Musashi remain fully available because KON is absent.
US_ISR: No dependable full-order-of-battle submarine contact on the Japanese main body is credited by 13T24; this advantage is temporary as the fleet prepares to enter the Philippine Sea.
next_focus: 14 Jun: old-battleship/close bombardment and final amphibious preparation around Saipan; Japanese fleet sortie east, first serious US submarine/air-search contact opportunities, and the changing carrier geometry before D-day.
